**Finding: compliant (at fallback) — no redline.**

The planner's hint that this rule was likely absent was wrong, so the key value here was catching §6.1 before concluding "no clause." There *is* an exclusivity covenant binding us — but it lands on the fallback rather than through it:

| Fallback element | §6.1 |
|---|---|
| Named competing product | ✅ Deerskin Products (narrowed by §1.1) + Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled |
| During term only | ✅ No post-term tail on us |
| Capped at 12 months | ⚠️ Term auto-renews, but coterminous and terminable by us on 90 days' notice |
| Carve-out | ⚠️ §6.2 closeout carve-out present; no internal-development/acquisition carve-out |

Two points worth flagging for the negotiation file even though they don't justify a redline on their own:

1. **The asymmetry runs in our favour.** §6.3 binds HDI for the term *plus two years* post-term, while our restriction stops at expiry. Reopening §6.1 invites HDI to reopen §6.3, which would be a bad trade for us.
2. **"Products substantially similar to" / "companies similar to"** is the one genuinely elastic phrase. It is anchored to named comparators so it isn't the undefined "any competing business" that would be walk-away, but if this agreement is being negotiated rather than reviewed as-signed, tightening that phrase to the named companies is a cheap, low-friction ask — and adding the internal-development/acquisition carve-out alongside it would move the clause to preferred.

I did not flag the §4.1 auto-renewal or the §4.2 Termination Payment, as those are term/exit economics that belong to other rules rather than this restrictive-covenant rule.
